vocabulary.meaning_en: a top with a collar and buttons
vocabulary.note_ar: يُقال غالباً على القميص الذي له ياقة وأزرار
vocabulary.example: He wore a white shirt to the interview.

vocabulary.meaning_en: clothing that covers each leg separately
vocabulary.note_ar: trousers بريطاني، pants أمريكي (وفي بريطانيا pants = ملابس داخلية). دائماً جمع: my trousers are
vocabulary.example: These trousers are too long for me.

vocabulary.meaning_en: women's clothing that hangs from the waist
vocabulary.example: She bought a long blue skirt.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a one-piece piece of women's clothing; to put on clothes
vocabulary.example: Get dressed, we're late!

vocabulary.meaning_en: a short, light coat
vocabulary.example: Take a jacket, it might get cold.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long, heavy piece of clothing worn over others in winter
vocabulary.example: It's snowing, so wear your coat.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a warm top, often made of wool
vocabulary.note_ar: من sweat = يعرق، لأنها ملابس ثقيلة تحفظ حرارة الجسم
vocabulary.example: My grandmother knitted me a sweater.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a simple top with short sleeves and no collar
vocabulary.note_ar: سُمّي كذلك لأنه يشبه حرف T عند فرده
vocabulary.example: I usually wear a T-shirt at home.

vocabulary.meaning_en: short trousers
vocabulary.example: It's hot, so I'm wearing shorts.

vocabulary.meaning_en: things you wear on your feet
vocabulary.example: Take off your shoes at the door.

vocabulary.meaning_en: soft sports shoes
vocabulary.example: I need new trainers for the gym.

vocabulary.meaning_en: open summer shoes with straps
vocabulary.example: I always wear sandals at the beach.

vocabulary.meaning_en: shoes that cover the ankle or part of the leg
vocabulary.example: These boots keep my feet dry in the rain.

vocabulary.meaning_en: soft things you wear on your feet inside shoes
vocabulary.example: I can't find a matching pair of socks.

vocabulary.meaning_en: something you wear on your head
vocabulary.example: Wear a hat in the sun.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long piece of cloth worn around the neck
vocabulary.example: She wrapped a scarf around her neck.

vocabulary.meaning_en: things you wear on your hands to keep them warm
vocabulary.example: My hands are cold; where are my gloves?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a strip worn around the waist
vocabulary.example: These trousers need a belt.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a long piece of cloth worn around the neck with a shirt; to fasten
vocabulary.note_ar: من الفعل tie = يربط: how to tie a tie
vocabulary.example: He wears a tie to work every day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: dark glasses that protect your eyes from the sun
vocabulary.example: Don't forget your sunglasses.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a woman's bag for small personal things
vocabulary.example: She put her phone in her handbag.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a bag you carry on your back
vocabulary.example: My backpack is full of books.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small case for money and cards
vocabulary.example: I keep my ID card in my wallet.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small clock you wear on your wrist
vocabulary.note_ar: ساعة الحائط = clock؛ و watch كفعل = يشاهد
vocabulary.example: My watch is five minutes fast.

vocabulary.meaning_en: jewellery worn on the ears
vocabulary.example: She wore gold earrings.

vocabulary.meaning_en: jewellery worn around the neck
vocabulary.example: He gave his mother a silver necklace.

vocabulary.meaning_en: jewellery worn on the finger; to make a bell sound
vocabulary.note_ar: The phone is ringing = الهاتف يرن
vocabulary.example: She has a diamond ring.

vocabulary.meaning_en: jewellery worn around the wrist
vocabulary.example: This bracelet was a gift from my sister.

vocabulary.meaning_en: special clothes that everyone in a group wears
vocabulary.example: Students must wear a school uniform.

vocabulary.meaning_en: popular styles of clothes at a certain time
vocabulary.example: She's very interested in fashion.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to say you will surely do something
vocabulary.example: I promise I'll call you tonight.

vocabulary.meaning_en: making you want to have or do something
vocabulary.example: The cakes in the window look so tempting.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to put on clothes to see if they fit
vocabulary.example: Can I try on this jacket?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give something to someone with your hand
vocabulary.example: She handed me the keys.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to hit your foot on something and almost fall
vocabulary.note_ar: over لأنك ترفع قدمك لتعبر فوق الشيء؛ trip كاسم = رحلة
vocabulary.example: I tripped over the cat in the dark.

vocabulary.meaning_en: nearly, but not completely
vocabulary.example: I almost missed the bus.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to choose or take something
vocabulary.example: Pick any colour you like.

vocabulary.meaning_en: soft and smooth like silk
vocabulary.example: She has long silky hair.

vocabulary.meaning_en: bright and reflecting light
vocabulary.example: He polished his shoes until they were shiny.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to shine with small flashes of light
vocabulary.note_ar: eyes sparkle at = تلمع العين انبهاراً بـ
vocabulary.example: Her eyes sparkled at the sight of the cake.

vocabulary.meaning_en: beautiful and stylish
vocabulary.example: She looked elegant in her black dress.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an amount of something kept for use; to provide
vocabulary.example: We have a month's supply of rice.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in a worried way
vocabulary.example: He laughed nervously.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to speak very quietly
vocabulary.example: She whispered the answer to her friend.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small room in a shop where you try on clothes
vocabulary.example: The fitting rooms are at the back of the store.

fine_lines.title: coat vs jacket
fine_lines.explanation_ar: coat أطول وأثقل، ونلبسه فوق الملابس في البرد الشديد أو المطر. jacket أقصر وأخف ويمكن لبسه في جو معتدل.

examples.sentence: Wear your heavy coat; it's freezing outside.
A light jacket is enough for a spring evening.

fine_lines.title: trousers vs pants
fine_lines.explanation_ar: الاثنتان معناهما بنطلون. trousers شائعة في بريطانيا، و pants شائعة في أمريكا. انتبه: في بريطانيا pants تعني الملابس الداخلية. والكلمتان دائماً بصيغة الجمع.

examples.sentence: My trousers are in the wash.

fine_lines.title: watch vs clock
fine_lines.explanation_ar: watch ساعة تلبسها في يدك (ومن معاني watch يراقب، فأنت تراقب بها الوقت). clock ساعة تُعلّق على الحائط أو توضع على الطاولة.

examples.sentence: He looked at his watch and left.
The clock on the wall stopped.

fine_lines.title: try on vs put on vs slip on
fine_lines.explanation_ar: try on تعني تقيس الملابس لترى هل تناسبك (عادة في المحل). put on تعني تلبس ملابسك عموماً. slip on تعني تلبس الشيء بسرعة وسهولة، كما نقول بالعربية «نطّ في البنطلون». لا تقل try on your coat عن معطفك الذي تملكه، بل put on your coat.

examples.sentence: She tried on three dresses before she chose one.
Put on your coat; it's cold outside.
He slipped on his shoes and ran out.

fine_lines.title: enter vs enter into
fine_lines.explanation_ar: enter وحدها معناها «يدخل إلى» مكاناً حقيقياً له حدود (متجر، غرفة، حديقة)، فلا نضع بعدها حرف جر. enter into تُستخدم للدخول المعنوي (يدخل في نقاش، اتفاق، شراكة). ويمكن أن تعبّر into عن اختراق سطح، مثل رصاصة تدخل في الحائط.

examples.sentence: She entered the store at ten o'clock.
The two companies entered into an agreement.
I entered into a long conversation with Sara.

expressions.example: On the other side of the street, there's a café.
I bought this funny hat just for fun.
You bought a year's supply of coffee!
I need a pair of gloves for the winter.
The child's eyes sparkled at the toys.
I got dressed quickly and left.

grammar.title: Adjective order: opinion before fact
grammar.explanation_ar: في الإنجليزية الصفة التي تعبّر عن رأيك (جميل، قديم، رائع) تأتي قبل الصفة التي تعبّر عن حقيقة (لون، مادة). لذلك نقول a beautiful red dress وليس a red beautiful dress، عكس العربية «فستان أحمر جميل».

grammar.title: Adjective / verb + verb-ing (describing a state)
grammar.explanation_ar: إذا جاء بعد صفة فعل، أو جاء فعلان وراء بعض مثل spend، فالفعل الثاني يأخذ ing ويصبح كالاسم، مهما كان زمن الجملة. فـ was busy picking ليست ماضياً مستمراً، بل تعني «كانت مشغولة بانتقاء».
examples: Sara was busy picking colourful socks.
He is busy reading a book.

grammar.title: Modal + base form, and when + subject vs while + -ing
grammar.explanation_ar: تذكير: بعد would وأخواتها يأتي الفعل في شكله الأساسي (would only buy). وبعد when إذا جاء فاعل نستخدم الفعل عادياً (when she tripped)، أما بعد while بدون فاعل فنضيف ing (while looking).
examples: She promised she would only buy a new shirt.
She laughed when she tripped over the boots.
She tripped while looking for sandals.

questions.question: Which is correct?
questions.explanation_ar: صفة الرأي beautiful تأتي قبل صفة الحقيقة red.

questions.question: She ___ the store at ten o'clock.
questions.explanation_ar: الدخول إلى مكان حقيقي = enter بدون حرف جر.

questions.question: The two companies ___ an agreement.
questions.explanation_ar: الدخول المعنوي في اتفاق = enter into.

questions.question: It's cold outside. ___ your coat.
questions.explanation_ar: تلبس ملابسك عموماً = put on، أما try on فللقياس في المحل.

questions.question: Sara was busy ___ colourful socks.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد الصفة busy يأخذ الفعل ing.

questions.question: A small clock you wear on your wrist is a:
questions.explanation_ar: watch = ساعة يد، clock = ساعة حائط.

questions.question: She almost tripped ___ a pair of boots.
questions.explanation_ar: trip over = يتعثر في (ترفع قدمك فوق الشيء).

questions.question: Which is usually longer and heavier?
